$schema.description: The JSON Schema an editor checks this file against.

origin.description: Origin serving the addresses that name no tenant — "/" and the deployment's own routes under /deployment — e.g. https://portal.example.com, scheme and host only with no trailing slash. Every tenant's own origin (PORTAL_TENANT_<ID>_PUBLIC_HOST) is trusted for authentication alongside it, and a request arriving on a host none of them names is answered under this one. Its scheme decides whether the deployment's session cookies are written as __Secure-, so every origin in the configuration has to share it.

defaultTenant.description: Tenant serving the addresses that name none of their own: "/", and a script run with no --tenant. Must name a configured tenant. Left out, "/" answers not-found and a visitor has to open an address naming a tenant.

maxConnections.description: Push deliveries in flight at once, and sockets held per push service. One agent serves the whole process, so this bounds the deployment. Defaults to 10.

maxBytes.description: Bytes the resized-image cache may occupy. One cache directory serves every tenant, so the budget is the deployment's.

sessionSecret.description: Signing and encryption secret for this tenant's sessions. Per tenant, not per deployment: each tenant authenticates through an instance of its own, so a secret that leaks forges sessions for that tenant alone. Generate a distinct long random value for every tenant (openssl rand -base64 32) — two tenants sharing one are refused.

routing.description: How this tenant's addresses are shaped. "path" (the default) carries the tenant id as the first path segment, e.g. https://portal.example.com/acme/sales, and the origin may be shared with other tenants. "host" drops that segment and lets PORTAL_TENANT_<ID>_PUBLIC_HOST name the tenant instead, e.g. https://acme.example.com/sales. "host" needs a host no other tenant is served on, and a proxy that sets X-Forwarded-Host (or Host) to the address the visitor used rather than the address of the server behind it — nginx sends its own upstream address by default, and a deployment left that way resolves no tenant and refuses every form submission. Changing this changes every address the tenant is reached at: the stored workspace URLs, the registered OAuth redirect URIs and the links already sent out all carry the old shape.

includeLanguage.description: Also load the base language (e.g. 'en' for 'en-US') in addition to the specific locale. Defaults to false.

url.description: Postgres connection URL of this tenant's own database. Every tenant has its own database; isolation is per-database.
Base URL of the AOS instance, e.g. https://erp.example.com/axelor-erp. Unique per tenant in topology A (dedicated AOS); shared across tenants in topology B (AOS multi-tenancy).

tenantId.description: AOS-side tenant id — independent of the portal tenant id. Set it when this tenant lives on a shared AOS instance with AOS multi-tenancy (topology B): every AOS call then carries X-Tenant-ID with this value. Leave unset for a dedicated AOS instance (topology A).

storage.description: The AOS instance's data.upload.dir base path (created on first connect; back it with a mounted volume so uploads survive). When PORTAL_TENANT_<ID>_AOS_TENANT_ID is set (topology B), the portal reads and writes files under <storage>/<tenantId> to match AOP's per-tenant subdirectory; a dedicated instance (topology A) uses this path as-is.

auth.description: AOS credentials: an API key (AOS 9+, generated in AOS under Preferences → API Keys), or a username and password for basic auth. The API key wins when both are set.

webhookSecret.description: Secret AOS uses to sign notification webhooks for this tenant. Set the same value in the AOS portal configuration.

live.description: true for live payments; defaults to sandbox.

paypal.description: PayPal merchant account. The browser needs the client id as well, under PORTAL_TENANT_<ID>_PUBLIC_PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID.

webhookSecret.description: Stripe webhook signing secret for this tenant's webhook endpoint. Without it, bank transfer is not offered at checkout.

legacyForwardUrl.description: Where to forward Up2Pay IPNs this tenant cannot attribute to a portal payment (legacy-ERP invoices, unknown context). Omit to not forward.

beneficiaryName.description: Name of the account a payment is credited to, at most 70 characters — the ISO 20022 limit for a creditor name. The value is sent as it stands, with nothing truncating it on the way out.

certsDir.description: Directory holding this tenant's mTLS client.crt and private-key.pem. Must be distinct per Hub PISP tenant — the certificate is the tenant's bank identity, so there is no shared default.

hubpisp.description: Hub PISP (BPCE) account. Register this tenant's webhook under this tenant's own path — /<tenantId>/api/webhooks/hubpisp/..., without the <tenantId> segment for a tenant reached on an origin of its own — so the webhook uses this tenant's credentials.

payments.description: Per-tenant merchant accounts. A provider a tenant omits is simply unavailable for that tenant.

port.description: TCP port the SMTP server listens on, commonly 587 for STARTTLS or 465 with secure set.

maxConnections.description: Connections this tenant's mail account may hold open at once. A mail server limits concurrency per sender, so the ceiling belongs to the account — a Microsoft 365 mailbox allows three. Tenants sharing a mailbox share one pool and one ceiling, so they must agree on this value or the configuration is refused at startup. Defaults to 10.

mattermost.description: Mattermost integration. The address the browser links to is browser-facing and lives under PORTAL_TENANT_<ID>_PUBLIC_MATTERMOST_HOST.

issuer.description: Keycloak realm issuer URL, with or without a trailing slash. Each tenant uses its own realm.

oauth.description: Per-tenant OAuth applications. Each provider is registered under the provider id '<provider>-<tenantId>' — register the matching redirect URI (/<tenantId>/api/auth/oauth2/callback/<provider>-<tenantId>, without the <tenantId> segment for a tenant reached on an origin of its own) with the identity provider. There is no global app: a tenant offers a provider only when it declares it here.

subject.description: mailto: address or https: URL identifying the sender to push services.

webPush.description: Web-push signing identity; the public key lives under PORTAL_TENANT_<ID>_PUBLIC_WEB_PUSH_PUBLIC_KEY. The service worker registers once per tenant — under the tenant path segment where several tenants share an origin, and at the root of the origin where the tenant has one to itself — so each tenant holds its own push subscription and its own key pair takes effect either way.

recordRetentionHours.description: How long terminal staged-upload records are kept before the prune sweep deletes them. Defaults to 168 (7 days).

host.description: Origin this tenant is served on, e.g. https://portal.example.com — scheme and host only, with no trailing slash. Workspace URLs are stored against it, every absolute link is built from it, and the deployment trusts it as an origin to authenticate on, so a tenant without one resolves no workspace. Tenants sharing an origin is the ordinary case; the scheme must be the one PORTAL_ORIGIN carries.

clientId.description: The PayPal client id the browser's checkout button is created with. Public by design; the secret stays in the payments group.

publicKey.description: The VAPID public key a browser subscribes with. Pairs with PORTAL_TENANT_<ID>_WEB_PUSH_PRIVATE_KEY; both are needed for notifications.

host.description: Mattermost address the sidebar links to.

buttonLabel.description: Text of the Keycloak sign-in button; defaults to "Log In with Keycloak".

buttonImage.description: Address of the image shown on the Keycloak sign-in button; defaults to the bundled Keycloak mark.

links.description: Social addresses the news application offers to share to.

public.description: Browser-facing settings for this tenant. Everything in this group is sent to every visitor; nothing outside it is.
